title: DNP3: Add TLS dissector
description:
IEEE 1815-2012[1] section 7.8 describes the use of DNP3 over TLS using TCP
port 19999. This commit creates a global to store the return of
`register_dissector` and then calls `ssl_dissector_add` in
`proto_reg_handoff_dnp3`.

[1] https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/servlet/opac?punumber=6327576

notes.body: approved this merge request
Confirmed that the port is registered with IANA, https://www.iana.org/assignments/service-names-port-numbers/service-names-port-numbers.xhtml?search=19999

I've only briefly scanned the changes, they seem to add only the DNP3 over UDP dissection to TLS, is that correct?

I think the existing udp handle was added to allow dissecting DNP3 over DTLS over UDP.  When using TLS, the underlying transport protocol is TCP so that would seem most appropriate entry point into the DNP3 dissector.

I'm also uncertain as to the steps to add support for a protocol over TLS, I had a quick look at packet-http.c and that seems to define the same entry point for both TCP and TLS, i.e. a dissect_http_on_stream() although there is some difference in the conversation data passed in.

Does the opendnp3 project provide sample captures, I wasn't able to locate them in their repo?

They provide code examples only. Here is a [capture.pcapng](/uploads/37792c977b50ea2c148e4a20cd3ccb6a/capture.pcapng) and the [premaster.txt](/uploads/db0956e64c5f7e3977078317ed036d4e/premaster.txt) to decrypt the traffic.

While capturing some packets to share here, I ran WS in a terminal and noticed some warnings on `stderr`, so the code is not correct. I marked this merge as WIP an will try to fix it.
marked this merge request as **draft**
I think that you should be adding the handle to the tls dissector using the `dnp3_tcp_handle`.

added 1 commit
  • 5174299c - [WIP] DNP3: Add TLS dissector
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/1864/diffs?diff_id=141227734&start_sha=f7c2a3a637667982c7879eb8154f9fe7d0b0edfb)

You are right. The segfault was because `create_dissector_handle` creates an anonymous dissector, using `create_dissector_handle_with_name` fixed that. Now I can call `ssl_dissector_add` with `dnp3_tcp_handle`, but I still get warnings:
> Warn Dissector bug, protocol DNP 3.0, in packet 42: epan/tvbuff.c:477: failed assertion "tvb && tvb->initialized"

It comes from the call to `tvb_captured_length` on `dissect_dnp3_al`, line 2957, and the assertion fail because `tvb` is NULL. I thought it would be a easy patch, but I guess nothing is easy when DNP3 is involved :)

I think the TLS decryption is working, the dissector bugs are occurring when there is more than one DNP3 PDU in a TCP segment and attempting to dissect PDU's after the first.  This works normally without TLS so I'm not sure what's going on here.
It's odder than I thought, not all TCP segments with multiple DNP3 PDU's are failing, e.g. frame 54.

I think that frame 54 doesn't fail because it is reassembled at 56. Other that fail (eg. 42, 48, 65) are reassembled at the same frame. The function that triggers the warning, `dissect_dnp3_al`, is only called if `pinfo->num==fragment_head->reassembled_in`.

I modified that code in commit a8ceeca444c to handle an issue with out of order application layer fragments over udp.  However I can't remember why I wrote the code that way.  I think it may have been an issue with application layer sequence number rolling over to 0 as well.

A lot has changed in `epan/reassemble.c` since then, but `process_reassembled_data` looks identical. Debugging a capture without TLS, `fragment_head->reas_in_layer_num` seems to be always 6. Maybe the layer didn't matter before?

Calling `dissect_dnp3_al` with `next_tvb` NULL will always trigger the warning, since the first argument is used unconditionally to call `tvb_captured_length`, but checking for NULL on line 3429 may be the wrong place to fix this. Could testing `pinfo->num` be a less strict way to prevent this, without masking future bugs that make `process_reassembled_data` return NULL? If that's the case, testing `pinfo->curr_layer_num`seems the best approach.

Anyway, a corner case like sequence-number-rollover-with-out-of-order-packets seems a sharp one. I would like to test if I haven't added a regression then, but I not sure how to recreate that case right now. Would you have a capture with something like that at hand?

I don't think this is particularly relevant to the issue as this is udp not tcp but anyway I've attached some files showing a failure to reassemble transport layer fragments due to sequence number rollover.  Note that these do not reassemble in the current dev release.  This is because the reassembly code expects a 32 bit sequence counter.  I had some push back in changes I proposed to support a smaller sequence counter.

[dnp3-al-frag-fail.pcapng](/uploads/52f46296bd70565697d38db5801b77ca/dnp3-al-frag-fail.pcapng) - udp fragments with transport sequence rollover, frags in order (63, 0, 1)

[dnp3-al-frag-fail2-re.pcapng](/uploads/9ec800b2dc2784eb08aa3f7eec2a8b82/dnp3-al-frag-fail2-re.pcapng) - as above but with out of order fragments, first and middle swapped (0, 63, 1)

[dnp3-al-frag-fail3-re.pcapng](/uploads/b7bf97e300d39299ec4391de53ebe748/dnp3-al-frag-fail3-re.pcapng) - as above but with out of order fragments middle and final swapped (63, 1, 0)

and another file with no rollover

[dnp3-udp-bad-order-frags2-re.pcapng](/uploads/c9701863cb31db697be2e17bbca11bc8/dnp3-udp-bad-order-frags2-re.pcapng) the first sequence incorrectly reassembled (seq 43-48, missing fragments 44 & 45) and the second sequence correctly reassembled (seq 51-55, with 54 and 54 swapped)

I was worried because the UDP dissector was also calling `dissect_dnp3_message`, but it looks like reassembly problems will make `frag_al` NULL, so the condition on line 3429 should not be relevant. Also, `pinfo->curr_layer_num` appears to change only when the TLS dissector is involved, it seems to be used for multiple TLS records in a single packet. So I think it's all good, thanks for providing the sample captures.

This seems a pretty uncommon API function, it is only used in one place.

Others such as packet-sip.c seems to use `register_dissector` from the `proto_register_xxx` function. The only difference appears that the latter results in the dissector being discoverable through something such as `find_dissector("dnp3.tcp")`.

Should `register_dissector` or `create_dissector_handle_with_name` be used?

My initial approach to this patch was to change as little as possible to dissect DNP3/TLS. Using the result of `create_dissector_handle` to call `ssl_dissector_add` causes WS to segfault accessing `dissector_handle_t->name`, so I had thought that `create_dissector_handle_with_name` should be used instead. Now that you point out how rare it's use is, I think `register_dissector` should be used. 

Actually, `register_dissector` is already used in `proto_register_dnp3`, but for UDP only, and it's return is discarded. Then `create_dissector_handle` is called for both dissectors in `proto_reg_handoff_dnp3` to obtain instances of `dissector_handle_t` to call `dissector_add_uint_with_preference`, etc. Other protocols (`packet-dns.c`, `packet-mbtcp.c`, `packet-sip.c`, etc.) appear to save the result of `register_dissector` in globals, which would make the calls to `create_dissector_handle` unnecessary.

changed this line in [version 5 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/1864/diffs?diff_id=142348920&start_sha=0aa5dab18d4522adeb21ef2513339594b7d3c47e#6c2400c14eada1efdfeaf250f6c6dfdd21d10b8b_4679_4680)

The register_dissector call was added to specifically allow DNP3 over something over UDP via Decode As, hence it only touched UDP.

I agree that it's probably best to do things similar to other protocols with the handles in static vars.
